comment.narrative: State Safety Roadmap Cambodia and a second ASEAN MS

Due to the travel restrictions caused by the COVID19 pandemic between 2020 and 2022 and the time pressure caused by the scheduling of the ICAO ICVM Audit to Cambodia in October 2023 the support to assess and improve the safety oversight capabilities of the AMS was focused on Cambodia.Cambodia was the AMS with lowest Effective Implementation index with an aviation system that due to its deeprooted deficiencies e.g. inspectors training policy on conflict of interest had the highest risk of receiving a Significant Safety Concern SSC. The support to the Civil Aviation Authority Secretary of State for Civil Aviation SSCA has assisted the country in the preparation of the ICAO ICVM audit identifying the most critical highest risk deficiencies to address and supporting the accomplishment of the Corrective Action Plan with a structured and exhaustive methodology.

comment.narrative: The support to the implementation of the Environmental Management Systems at airport level comes from the positive outcomes from the assistance provided by the EUSEA Aviation Partnership Project EUSEA APP to CAAT and the officials in Trat Airport Thailand. The Project picked up the initiative with the intention to regionalise it among the AMS and to consolidate an implementation package that could support any other AMS airport to launch the EMS implementation confidently.The Project has supported the implementation of the EMS in Luang Prabang Laos PDR Iloilo and Bohol Airports Philippines and Da Nang Vietnam. comment.narrative: 8 ASEAN MS actively contributing to the AFOSA programme

Since the operationalisation of the AFOSA Programme 6 AMS have submitted ramp inspections of foreign operators as per the AFOSA procedures. However the number of AMS continuously providing ramp inspections is lower 34. The support of the project through technical workshops to explore the adoption of the European Ramp Inspection programme tools and best practices by AFOSA has resulted in a revigorated programme and in a more harmonised ramp inspection set of procedures among the AMS. However the number of AMS regularly contributing with ramp inspections safety related data remains the same at the closure of the project 6 AMS. In order to achieve the active involvement of all the AMS in the AFOSA programme it is necessary to link it to higher level policies at ASEAN or ASEANEU level.
